card.title: The part that made clocks tick

panels.text: Water clocks and sundials are possibly the oldest time-measuring instruments.
Around 1300 in Europe, a new idea made the first mechanical clocks possible: the verge escapement.
Water-driven clock mechanisms were adapted to run on falling weights. An oscillating part, probably derived from bell-ringing or alarm devices, controlled how that power was released.

That controlled release of power is the escapement. These clocks needed no water or mercury, and were meant for signalling, such as timing services and public events, and for modelling the Solar System.

probes.question: What does an escapement do in a mechanical clock?
options: Releases the clock's power in small controlled steps
